title: Write Addressability under Superposition
hypothesis: A neural system can learn a sparse functional coordinate system from dense superposition and use an inferred, aligned write address to update a shared latent function with substantially less off-target interference than an otherwise identical sparse model using global writer optimization.

scope.primary_claim: This is a mechanism test for learned functional read/write coordinates, not a language-model benchmark or evidence that SAE-style coordinates are the final architecture.

world.observation_equation: x = A s with fixed dense column-normalized Gaussian A

model.candidate: top-k sparse functional encoder + linear writer
model.decisive_baseline: same pretrained sparse model and frozen encoder, but ordinary SGD updates the entire writer

editing.address_inference: For each latent q, solve the least-squares residual r_i ~= z_iq delta_q and choose the valid q with minimum residual error.
editing.inferred_write: Only the inferred writer column is changed by the least-squares delta.
editing.oracle_address: Evaluator-only diagnostic: map each true feature to its most correlated learned latent on a held-out probe set.
editing.permutation_control: Inference is unchanged; only the inferred read-address -> write-destination mapping is cyclically permuted.

evaluation.mechanistic_proxy: Q = E_I[z_q^2] / E_A[s_j^2], predicting L up to write-magnitude fit error
evaluation.retention: After each edit, evaluate all retained probes from earlier edited atoms against the evaluator's current V. Retention probes are never used for optimization.

diagnostic_sweep.role: Descriptive capacity-boundary diagnostic. It is not part of the frozen primary pass/fail gate in v1.

interpretation_limits: A positive result establishes the mechanism only in the synthetic additive sparse-functional world used here.
The Gaussian mixing matrix is intentionally favorable to sparse recovery; structured and correlated superposition is a later validation.
The learned encoder is frozen during edits, so this experiment does not test continual creation or reorganization of the functional basis.
The decisive causal comparison is inferred addressed write versus global writer SGD from the exact same pretrained sparse model. Dense and MoE baselines are contextual.
Ground-truth s, A, V, and target feature ids are evaluator-only. Any use of them by the inferred-address editor invalidates the experiment.
Failure of a contextual baseline to learn the base world cannot be counted as evidence for write addressability.
Failure rejects this frozen v1 mechanism test; it does not prove that no alternative addressable architecture can work.
